ACTION: ADD
TITLE: KL-Regularized Fine-Tuning with Trajectory Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose to fine-tune the pre-trained diffusion model using a KL-regularized objective, where the regularization term is based on the KL divergence between entire denoising trajectories, rather than the marginal KL divergence. We will consider a variant of the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm to minimize the loss function, which includes a trajectory KL regularization term. Specifically, we will use the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.001 and a batch size of 64. Additionally, we will experiment with different levels of KL regularization strength (α in the paper) to study its impact on the quality of the fine-tuned model.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method with the KL-unregularized case (ignoring the KL term) and the traditional KL regularization method (using the marginal KL divergence).
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed method to outperform the KL-unregularized case and the traditional KL regularization method, especially for more complex tasks like text-to-image generation and document layout generation. However, we predict that a very high level of KL regularization strength may lead to suboptimal results.

Note: This proposal is motivated by the common practice of relaxing the KL regularization term to the trajectory KL constraint due to the intractability of the marginal KL divergence for diffusion models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging the Multi-Step Generative Structure for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the potential of the multi-step generative structure of diffusion and flow models for fine-tuning. Specifically, we will explore the following: (1) residual connection-based fine-tuning, where the output of the pre-trained model is used as input to the fine-tuned model; (2) recurrence for fine-tuning, where the fine-tuned model is trained to predict the noise schedule at each step; and (3) use of partial information from previous steps to condition the fine-tuned model. We will experiment with different levels of residual connection strength, recurrence depth, and information aggregation schemes to evaluate their impact on fine-tuning performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed methods with the standard fine-tuning approach and the KL-regularized fine-tuning method proposed in proposal 1.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed methods to improve the fine-tuning performance, especially for tasks like molecule generation that involve multiple steps of transformation.

Note: This proposal leverages the generative structure of diffusion and flow models to improve fine-tuning. We hypothesize that incorporating previous information or using residual connections can help the fine-tuned model converge faster to the optimal solution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flow-Based Fine-Tuning for Error Correction
PROPOSAL: We propose a flow-based approach to fine-tune the pre-trained flow model for error correction. Specifically, we will train a flow model to transform the samples generated by the pre-trained model back to the target data distribution. We will use a combination of the Sinkhorn divergence and the Wasserstein distance as the loss function to measure the difference between the pre-trained model and the target distribution. Additionally, we will incorporate a regularization term to prevent overfitting and ensure that the fine-tuned flow model produces samples with similar quality to the pre-trained model.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method with standard fine-tuning using KL-regularization and the proposed KL-regularized fine-tuning method.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed method to effectively correct the errors of the pre-trained flow model, especially for tasks like text-to-image generation where the quality of the generated samples is critical.

Note: This proposal is motivated by the fact that flow models are well-suited for density estimation and can be used to correct errors in the pre-trained model.

Revision of the PRIVATE NOTE: be particularly clear about how these high estimates will be handled when final results are reported.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: KL-Regularized Fine-Tuning with Trajectory Regularization
REVISED PROPOSAL: We refine our previous proposal by incorporating the Flow-Based Fine-Tuning for Error Correction approach as a pre-processing step to correct the errors in the pre-trained model. Specifically, we will first fine-tune the pre-trained model using the KL-regularized objective with trajectory regularization (proposal 1), and then apply the flow-based approach (proposal 3) to correct any remaining errors. This two-stage process will allow the model to learn the target distribution with higher accuracy and robustness.
CONTROLS: We will compare our revised method with the original KL-regularized fine-tuning approach (proposal 1) and the flow-based approach (proposal 3) applied separately.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: We expect our revised method to achieve better results than the original KL-regularized fine-tuning approach and better error correction than the flow-based approach applied separately.

Note: This revised proposal combines the strengths of the two previous proposals to obtain a more robust and accurate fine-tuned model.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Leveraging the Multi-Step Generative Structure for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We refine our previous proposal by incorporating a dual objectives approach, where the fine-tuned model is trained to maximize the reward while minimizing the KL divergence between the pre-trained model and the fine-tuned model. We will use a weighted sum of the two objectives to balance the trade-off between reward maximization and KL regularization. Additionally, we will experiment with different levels of weight assigned to the KL regularization term to study its impact on fine-tuning performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method with the standard fine-tuning approach and the KL-regularized fine-tuning method.
COST: 2200
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed method to achieve better results than the standard fine-tuning approach and the KL-regularized fine-tuning method, especially for tasks like molecule generation where the quality of the generated samples is critical.

Note: This revised proposal aims to address the initial value function bias problem by incorporating a KL regularization term into the reward maximization objective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rejection Sampling for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to adapt the rejection sampling approach, previously studied for autoregressive models, to the fine-tuning of diffusion models. Specifically, we will sample multiple trajectories from the pre-trained model, rank them based on their rewards, and then train the model to produce only the top-ranked trajectories. We will use a learning rate schedule to adapt the rejection threshold and study its impact on fine-tuning performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method with the standard fine-tuning approach, KL-regularized fine-tuning, and Best-of-N sampling.
COST: 2800
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed method to achieve better results than the standard fine-tuning approach and comparable results to KL-regularized fine-tuning, especially for tasks like text-to-image generation where the quality of the generated samples is critical.

Note: This proposal aims to leverage the rejection sampling approach to efficiently select high-reward samples for fine-tuning, potentially improving the quality of the generated samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-Agnostic Fine-Tuning for Flow Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a reward-agnostic fine-tuning approach for flow models that uses the differences in the density estimates of the pre-trained and fine-tuned models as the objective function. Specifically, we will compute the Sinkhorn divergence between the two densities and optimize the fine-tuned model to minimize this divergence. We will also study the impact of different regularization techniques, such as weight decay and early stopping, to prevent overfitting.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method with standard fine-tuning, KL-regularized fine-tuning, and flow-based fine-tuning for error correction.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed method to achieve comparable results to the standard fine-tuning approach and potentially better results for tasks where the accurate density estimate is crucial, such as molecule generation.

Note: This proposal aims to leverage the density estimation capabilities of flow models to correct errors in the pre-trained model without relying on explicit rewards.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Auto-Augmentation for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose an auto-augmentation approach to fine-tune diffusion models, where we adapt an auto-augmentation policy to perturb the inputs to the pre-trained model during fine-tuning. Specifically, we will train a reinforcement learning agent to find the optimal perturbation strategy that maximizes the reward and minimizes the KL divergence between the pre-trained and fine-tuned models.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method with standard fine-tuning, KL-regularized fine-tuning, and leveraging the multi-step generative structure for fine-tuning.
COST: 3800
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed method to improve the fine-tuning performance, especially for tasks like document layout generation where the auto-augmentation policy can help improve the model's robustness to noisy inputs.

Note: This proposal aims to leverage the reinforcement learning capabilities to adapt the auto-augmentation policy to the specific task and pre-trained model, potentially improving the quality of the fine-tuned model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose an adversarial training approach to fine-tune diffusion models, where we train a discriminator to distinguish between the samples generated by the pre-trained model and the fine-tuned model. The discriminator's loss is used as an additional regularization term for the fine-tuned model. We will study the impact of different adversarial learning strategies, such as the hinge loss and the cosine similarity, on the fine-tuning performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method with standard fine-tuning, KL-regularized fine-tuning, and leveraging the multi-step generative structure for fine-tuning.
COST: 4200
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed method to improve the fine-tuning performance, especially for tasks like text-to-image generation where the pre-trained model's samples may not align well with the target distribution.

Note: This proposal aims to leverage the adversarial learning capabilities to improve the fine-tuning performance by encouraging the fine-tuned model to generate samples that are more diverse and plausible.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensemble Methods for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to explore the use of ensemble methods to combine the predictions of multiple fine-tuned diffusion models. Specifically, we will train multiple fine-tuned models using different fine-tuning strategies, and then combine their predictions using techniques such as averaging, stacking, and voting. We will study the impact of different ensemble methods on the fine-tuning performance and compare our results with the baseline fine-tuning approaches.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method with standard fine-tuning, KL-regularized fine-tuning, leveraging the multi-step generative structure for fine-tuning, flow-based fine-tuning for error correction, rejection sampling for diffusion models, reward-agnostic fine-tuning for flow models, auto-augmentation for diffusion models, and adversarial training for fine-tuning diffusion models.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed method to achieve the best results among all the fine-tuning approaches, especially for tasks like molecule generation where the ensemble methods can help improve the model's robustness and accuracy.

Note: This proposal aims to leverage the ensemble methods to combine the strengths of different fine-tuning approaches and achieve better results than any individual fine-tuning approach.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trajectory KL Divergence Relaxation for KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: Investigate whether a KL divergence relaxation between entire denoising trajectories can be used as a more effective and stable alternative to ignoring KL regularization, despite its subpar performance in previous work. We will analyze this using a fine-tuned version of the DDPM model (Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models) on the LSUN dataset, which is a challenging benchmark for diffusion models.
CONTROLS: Ignore KL regularization, use only the reward maximization objective to highlight potential instability, and compare with the baseline KL regularization on the pre-trained model's marginal distribution.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: This approach may result in moderate performance improvements but will likely struggle with the initial value function bias problem, leading to suboptimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rejection Sampling for Diffusion Models with KL Regularization
PROPOSAL: Adapt rejection sampling methods (such as RSO, RAFT, and Reinforce-Rej) to incorporate KL regularization towards the pre-trained diffusion model. We will consider how this can be done using a KL divergence upper bound between entire denoising trajectories, and experiment with different sampling strategies to balance the trade-off between reward maximization and adherence to the pre-trained model. This will be evaluated on a fine-tuned version of the DDPM model on the ImageNet dataset.
CONTROLS: Compare with baseline rejection sampling without KL regularization and with the previous Trajectory KL Divergence Relaxation approach.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: This approach might show promising results, particularly when fine-tuning models on more complex datasets, but could also struggle with optimizing the KL regularization term.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Differentiable Sampling for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Explore whether leveraging the differentiable nature of the sampling process in diffusion models can lead to more effective KL regularization. We will implement a custom sampling procedure that allows for backpropagation of gradients through the sampling process, and use this to introduce a gradient-based objective for KL regularization. This will be tested on a fine-tuned version of the DDPM model on the CIFAR-10 dataset, with a focus on how well this approach generalizes to larger datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline KL regularization approach and with the rejection sampling approach.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: This approach might provide significant performance improvements, especially when combined with rejection sampling, but could also be computationally expensive and challenging to implement.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Improving Differentiable Sampling for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Expand the custom sampling procedure to incorporate more advanced techniques, such as polynomial interpolation or Riemannian optimization, to further improve the quality of the KL regularization. We will also extend the implementation to support multiple diffusion models and evaluate the method's performance on more challenging datasets, such as the ImageNet dataset.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline KL regularization approach, the rejection sampling approach, and the previous Trajectory KL Divergence Relaxation approach.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: This approach may lead to further performance improvements, but might also introduce additional computational overhead and complexity, making it harder to scale to larger models and datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adapting Diffusion Models for Text-to-Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Adapt the proposed methods for fine-tuning diffusion models to the domain of text-to-image generation, where the rewards are known to be poorly correlated with the marginal likelihoods of the generated images. We will experiment with these methods on a text-to-image conditional diffusion model, and evaluate their performance using metrics such as Inception Score and FID Score.
CONTROLS: Compare with baseline text-to-image models, such as the text-to-image diffusion model proposed in the paper "Diffusion-Based Image Synthesis with Depth and Normal Estimation."
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: This approach may be particularly challenging due to the complex nature of text-to-image generation, and could result in suboptimal performance. However, it may also reveal interesting insights into the limitations of current fine-tuning methods for diffusion models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Structural Regularization for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Explore the idea of leveraging the structural properties of diffusion models to introduce additional regularization techniques, such as `conditioning' on the intermediate noise states or leveraging the flow-based structure of the diffusion model. We will experiment with these ideas on a fine-tuned version of the DDPM model on the CIFAR-10 dataset and evaluate their performance using metrics such as the Fooling Rate and the Mean Squared Error.
CONTROLS: Compare with baseline KL regularization approaches and with rejection sampling approach.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: This approach has potential to yield novel and challenging insights into the structure of diffusion models, and might also lead to more robust fine-tuning methods, but could also be computationally expensive and require substantial expertise in model analysis.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-Free Fine-Tuning for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the possibility of fine-tuning diffusion models without explicit reward feedback, using only samples from the data distribution. We will explore different techniques for bootstrapping rewards, such as exploiting the interpolation property of flow-based models or leveraging the information contained in the initial noise. This will be evaluated on a fine-tuned version of the DDPM model on the ImageNet dataset and assessed using metrics such as the Frechet Inception Distance (FID) and the Inception Score (IS).
CONTROLS: Compare with baseline fine-tuning approaches that use explicit reward feedback, such as PPO.
COST: 24000
PREDICTION: This approach may lead to significant performance improvements, especially in scenarios where explicit reward feedback is difficult or impractical to obtain, but could also be challenging to implement and might require identification of meaningful bootstrapping rewards.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unifying KL-Regularized Reward Maximization and Rejection Sampling
PROPOSAL: Investigate the theoretical connection between KL-regularized reward maximization and rejection sampling, and explore whether these two approaches can be unified under a common framework. We will develop a theoretical analysis of the relationships between these two methods and provide a convergence guarantee for their combined approach. This will be evaluated through a series of theoretical experiments on the performance of the unified approach.
CONTROLS: Compare with baseline approaches that are based solely on either KL-regularized reward maximization or rejection sampling.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: This approach may lead to a deeper understanding of the relationships between KL-regularized reward maximization and rejection sampling, and could potentially yield more efficient and more robust fine-tuning methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Case Studies on Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models for Real-World Textual and Image Generation Tasks
PROPOSAL: Apply the proposed fine-tuning methods for diffusion models to several real-world textual and image generation tasks, including document layout generation, molecule generation, and text-to-image generation. We will use datasets such as the Document Layout Generation dataset, the Mater refugees dataset and the COCO dataset, and evaluate the performance of the proposed methods using metrics such as the Frechet Inception Distance (FID) score, the Inception score and the Bijectivation marginal likelihood.
CONTROLS: Compare with baseline approaches that use traditional fine-tuning methods.
COST: 48000
PREDICTION: This approach may yield practical insights into the performance of the proposed fine-tuning methods in real-world scenarios and help establish their usefulness for downstream tasks, but could also require significant expertise in the involved applications.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Novel KL-Regularization Technique for Diffusion Models via Variational Inference
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel KL-Regularization technique for fine-tuning diffusion models by utilizing a hierarchical variational inference approach. Given a pre-trained diffusion model and a reward function, we introduce a variational distribution over the entire conditional denoising process. By maximizing the variational lower-bound, we optimize the reward while maintaining a valid distribution that is close to the pre-trained reference model. This method is tractable and avoids the intractable marginal likelihoods, addressing the major challenge in KL-Regularized fine-tuning for diffusion models.
CONTROLS: Baseline: KL-Regularization without variational inference (trajectory KL divergence); Ablation: No KL-Regularization (only reward maximization)
COST: 360
PREDICTION: This approach should significantly improve fine-tuning accuracy and stability, but it may require careful tuning of the variational parameters to avoid mode collapse.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Flow-based Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the structure of diffusion and flow models, we propose a novel regularization term based on flows, which encourages the fine-tuned model to preserve the underlying data distribution. By constructing an invertible transformation that targets the distribution difference between the pre-trained and fine-tuned models, we effectively leverage the multi-step generative structure to enhance fine-tuning quality.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Traditional KL-Regularization (trajectory KL divergence); Ablation: No regularization
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Flow-based regularization should improve fine-tuning performance and provide a more interpretable understanding of the learned distribution. However, its effectiveness might be sensitive to the choice of flow architecture and optimization hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Instance-aware Reward Shaping for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: To better leverage the rewards for specific instances, we propose a novel instance-aware reward shaping technique. By identifying the most relevant segments of the sampled denoising trajectory for each instance, we create a task-specific reward signal that promotes desirable behaviors in the fine-tuned model. This approach is particularly useful for tasks like document layout generation, where structure and composition matter.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard reward function; Ablation: No instance-aware reward shaping
COST: 540
PREDICTION: Instance-aware reward shaping should lead to improved fine-tuning accuracy and quality, especially for complex tasks like document layout generation. However, it may require significant additional computation for reward calculation and instance segmentation.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Unsupervised Fine-tuning of Flow Models via Density Matching
PROPOSAL: For correcting errors in pre-trained flow models without explicit rewards, we propose an unsupervised fine-tuning method based on density matching. By leveraging the underlying structure of flow models and the available samples from the data distribution, we regularize the fine-tuned model to match the target density. This approach can correct discretization and statistical errors, leading to improved sample quality.
CONTROLS: Baseline: No fine-tuning; Ablation: Fine-tuning without density matching
COST: 720
PREDICTION: Density matching should effectively improve sample quality, but its convergence may be sensitive to the choice of divergence metric and optimization hyperparameters.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: REVISED Unsupervised Fine-tuning of Flow Models via Density Matching
PROPOSAL: We refine the unsupervised fine-tuning method by incorporating a multi-scale density matching approach. Rather than targeting a single density, we define a hierarchy of densities corresponding to different levels of abstraction in the generated samples. By matching the target density at multiple scales, we encourage the fine-tuned model to capture both local and global properties of the target data distribution.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Original density matching method; Ablation: Fine-tuning without multi-scale density matching
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Multi-scale density matching should provide more robust and effective corrections, reducing the risk of over-smoothing the data distribution. However, it may require additional computational resources for density matching at multiple scales.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Analyzing the Initial Value Function Bias in KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: We investigate the initial value function bias problem in KL-Regularized reward maximization for diffusion models. By providing a theoretical analysis and experimental evidence, we demonstrate the importance of this bias and propose methods to mitigate it. Our results highlight the practical implications of this bias and suggest strategies for addressing it in future work.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard KL-Regularized reward maximization; Ablation: Reward maximization without KL-Regularization
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Understanding and addressing the initial value function bias will be crucial for future research in KL-Regularized reward maximization. This work should provide valuable insights and methods for improving the performance of fine-tuning diffusion models.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Benchmarking Fine-tuning Methods for Diffusion Models on Text-to-Image Generation
PROPOSAL: We conduct an extensive benchmarking study to evaluate the effectiveness of various fine-tuning methods for diffusion models on text-to-image generation tasks. By using a suite of commonly used datasets and metrics, we compare the performance of novel KL-Regularization, flow-based regularization, instance-aware reward shaping, and unsupervised fine-tuning methods. Our findings provide a thorough understanding of the strengths and limitations of each approach and inform the design of future fine-tuning methods.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Original diffusion model; Comparison: Other fine-tuning methods (e.g., rejection sampling, best-of-N sampling)
COST: 1080
PREDICTION: This benchmarking study will provide valuable insights into the performance of fine-tuning methods on text-to-image generation tasks, but it may require significant computational resources due to the generation of high-quality images.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Flow-based Regularization for Diffusion Models on Document Layout Generation
PROPOSAL: We extend the flow-based regularization approach to document layout generation tasks, where the generated layouts must adhere to specific structural constraints. By incorporating a document-level flow that accounts for these constraints, we demonstrate improved fine-tuning performance and better adherence to the target layout distributions.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard KL-Regularized reward maximization; Ablation: Flow-based regularization without document-level flow
COST: 720
PREDICTION: This extension should improve the performance of flow-based regularization on document layout generation tasks, but it may require additional computational resources for learning the document-level flow.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Hybrid Approach to Fine-tuning Diffusion Models for Molecule Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a hybrid approach that combines the strengths of KL-Regularization, flow-based regularization, and unsupervised fine-tuning for molecule generation tasks. By leveraging the strengths of each method, we aim to improve the quality and diversity of the generated molecules while reducing the risk of overfitting to the target data distribution.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard KL-Regularized reward maximization; Comparison: Individual methods (KL-Regularization, flow-based regularization, unsupervised fine-tuning)
COST: 1440
PREDICTION: This hybrid approach should improve the performance of fine-tuning diffusion models on molecule generation tasks, but it may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: ADD 9
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Flow-based Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of flow-based regularization for diffusion models, developing bounds on the convergence rate of the fine-tuning process and characterizing the impact of the regularization strength on the resulting distribution. Our results provide a comprehensive understanding of the algorithmic properties of flow-based regularization and offer insights into its potential limitations.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: This theoretical analysis should provide a solid foundation for the understanding and development of flow-based regularization methods, but it may require significant mathematical expertise to derive and interpret the theoretical results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating KL-Regularized Reward Maximization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will perform experiments on fine-tuning diffusion models using KL-regularized reward maximization with proxy losses, trained on popular benchmarks in text-to-image generation (LSUN), document layout generation (NLVR), and molecule generation (Zinc). We compare against the baseline of ignoring KL regularization and against using the trajectory KL diversity in each experiment. Models are trained using the EDM [1] diffusion model, Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD) with Adam optimizer, and KL loss upper-bounded by the MSE (Mean Squared Error) between denoising trajectory paths.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: model fine-tuned without KL regularization; Baseline 2: KL regularization using trajectory paths only (without proxy losses); Ablation 1: different values of KL regularization strength.
COST: 43200
PREDICTION: We expect that using proxy losses to upper-bound the KL divergence will outperform ignoring KL regularization, and that the results will be closer to those of using the exact KL divergence when we increase the KL regularization strength. However, we hypothesize that higher values of KL regularization strength might lead to model instability issues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Trajectory KL Regularization on Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We extend Proposal 1 by analyzing the effect of adding trajectory KL regularization to the reward maximization objective, where the KL divergence between entire denoising trajectories is used. We compare experimentally against the baseline of ignoring KL regularization, the exact KL divergence (upper-bounded by proxy losses in Proposal 1), and against using trajectory KL regularization on the reversed diffusion process.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 2 from Proposal 1; Ablation 2: different levels of reverse process regularization.
COST: 69120
PREDICTION: We expect that the performance improvement of using trajectory KL regularization will vary depending on the specific task and the initial value of the reverse process, and that the regularization of the reversed diffusion process will be crucial when reverse process initialization is near the optimal but noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging Sampling Structure for Efficient Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We investigate whether the intermediate noisy states in the diffusion process can be used as input to different reward functions or used as auxiliary components for optimization. We use this structure to propose two new methods for fine-tuning diffusion models: (1) 'Noise-Aware' reward function that takes into account the intermediate noise level and (2) 'State-Aware' optimization where intermediate noisy states are used to compute an auxiliary objective that encourages smooth transitions between them.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 3 from Proposals 1 and 2; Ablation 3: combination of noise-aware rewards with baseline methods.
COST: 103680
PREDICTION: We expect that the noise-aware reward function will outperform baseline methods for tasks where the intermediate noise levels are informative about the generated samples, while the state-aware optimization will be more beneficial for tasks where the smoothness of generated samples is important.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Turning Flow Models Without Explicit Rewards
PROPOSAL: We explore the possibility of correcting the errors of a pre-trained flow model by fine-tuning it using only samples from the data distribution and without explicit rewards. We propose a ' Contrastive Learning' method that encourages the pre-trained model to generate samples that are closer to the data distribution by minimizing the reconstruction loss of the generated samples and the KL divergence between the pre-trained and the target data distributions.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 2 from Proposal 1; Ablation 4: varying levels of target data distribution diversity.
COST: 129600
PREDICTION: We expect that the contrastive learning method will be effective in reducing the error of the pre-trained flow model, especially when the target data distribution is structurally simple. However, we anticipate that this will come at the cost of reduced sample quality, and that methods that balance fine-tuning with generative sample quality will be crucial.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Fine-Turning Flow Models Without Explicit Rewards
PROPOSAL: We modify Proposal 4 to use an additional 'data-driven' approach that corrects the errors of a pre-trained flow model by fine-tuning it using only samples from the data distribution and without explicit rewards. This approach involves learning a 'policy' in the learned flow to correct the bias in the initial noise distribution of the pre-trained model. We scaffold the policy learning process using a series of 'baby' policies that progressively introduce the learned corrections back to the initial noise distribution.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 2 from Proposal 1; Ablation 4: varying levels of policy complexity and scaffolded learning.
COST: 172800
PREDICTION: We expect that the refined approach will be more effective than Proposal 4 in reducing the error of the pre-trained flow model, especially when the target data distribution is structurally complex.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Investigating KL-Regularized Reward Maximization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We modify Proposal 1 to include an analysis of the sensitivity of the KL-regularized reward maximization to the choice of proxy loss function. We compare the performance of using mean squared error (MSE), cross entropy (CE), and differentiable sufficient statistics (DSS) as proxy losses. Additionally, we investigate the effect of different numbers of training steps on the KL-regularized reward maximization.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 2 from Proposal 1; Ablation 5: varying levels of training steps and proxy loss functions.
COST: 207360
PREDICTION: We expect that using DSS as a proxy loss will be more effective than MSE and CE, especially when the target data distribution has complex structural dependencies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Relationship Between Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning and Policy Gradient Methods
PROPOSAL: We investigate the connection between the diffusion model fine-tuning methods and policy gradient methods. We demonstrate that by viewing the diffusion model as a policy that samples from the target distribution, we can view the KL-regularized reward maximization as a form of policy gradient method. We compare the performance of this policy gradient method with existing diffusion model fine-tuning methods and analyze the conditions under which the policy gradient method converges to the optimal policy.
CONTROLS: Baselines 1 and 2 from Proposal 1; Ablation 6: varying levels of policy gradient step sizes.
COST: 259200
PREDICTION: We expect that the policy gradient method will outperform existing diffusion model fine-tuning methods when the target data distribution is structurally complex, especially when the policy gradient step sizes are carefully tuned.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analysis of Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning for Real-World Applications
PROPOSAL: We evaluate the performance of the proposed diffusion model fine-tuning methods on a set of real-world benchmarks in text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation. We compare the performance of the proposed methods with state-of-the-art baselines and analyze the results to identify the strengths and weaknesses of each method in real-world scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the reliability of RAG-based hallucination detection using anchor tasks
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we use three anchor tasks, fact-checking, evidence-based reasoning, and correcting a misleading statement, to assess the quality of hallucination detection in RAG systems. We fine-tune a set of pre-trained LLMs on each anchor task and evaluate their performance in detecting hallucinations in RAG responses. We measure the agreement between the human annotations and the model predictions using Cohen's kappa statistic and the Fleiss' kappa for inter-rater reliability. We use a diverse set of human annotators and consider their agreements as ground truth. Controls: standard RAG models with no hallucination detection. We compare our results with ReDeEP and the follow-up work. COST: 5000. PREDICTION: We expect to see significant agreement between the human annotations and the model predictions, especially for fine-tuned LLMs, which indicates that our approach is effective in detecting hallucinations. Potential conflicts might arise from the complexity of the anchor tasks, as they require a specific type of common sense, which might not be consistently acquired by the models.

TITLE: Quantifying Internal Knowledge Utilization with Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel method that leverages contrastive learning to quantify an LLM's internal knowledge utilization during generation. By leveraging two types of positive pairs, one formed around the generated response and another around a paraphrased version of the response, and a negative pair formed around the response and the paraphrased text, we can model the internal knowledge utilization as a similarity score between the two positive pairs. We train and test various classical DFF methods with focal stacks sampled at different densities (e.g., 10, 20, 40 frames per focal sweep) and measure their performance in terms of depth accuracy and completeness. Specifically, we use the metrics of the NYU v2 depth benchmark ( $\delta_1$ and $\delta_2$ ) and compare the results to that of using a fixed, high-density sampling schedule (e.g., the 60-frame sampling schedule used in the original work of Park et al. [1]). We then analyze our results to identify the minimum required sampling density for DFF methods to achieve satisfactory performance and investigate the trade-offs between sampling density, model complexity, and computational efficiency.
CONTROLS: The fixed-density sampling schedule (60 frames), Laplacian-based DFF, frequency-domain contrast-based DFF as baselines.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: We expect to find that increasing sampling density improves depth accuracy and completeness for DFF methods up to a certain point, beyond which the benefits diminish due to the increasing noise and computational cost associated with higher sampling rates. However, the exact asymptote will depend on the specific method and dataset. Failure to capture complex depth structures with high-frequency content in scenes may indicate that our sampling density threshold is suboptimal.

Note: [1] Park et al. (2005) - http://www.cs.brown.edu/~zxie/papers/GrabCut_Hon06.pdf

TITLE: Physics-Informed Depth Estimation with Multi-Max Transformation
PROPOSAL: We propose a learning-based DFF model, termed Physics-Informed Depth Estimation (PI-DE), that explicitly incorporates the physical form of the focus response of light in a camera. PI-DE learns a multi-max transformation that maps the focus stack to a latent space, where the depth information is encoded in a manner consistent with the underlying physics of focusing. Specifically, we define the multi-max transformation as a learnable function that predicts a mode of the focus response, which we then use to compute a depth-aware focal feature map. This feature map is then fed into a depth decoder to produce a refined depth map.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art learning-based DFF models, such as the self-supervised model of [2] and the hybrid model of [3], as baselines.
COST: 1620
PREDICTION: We expect PI-DE to outperform existing learning-based DFF models by capturing the physical relationships between focus and depth, particularly in scenes with complex textures and depth structures. However, PI-DE may struggle with fine textures and reflective regions where the focus response is ambiguous, leading to lower depths accuracy in these areas.

Note: [2] Srinivasan et al. (2020) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.10582, [3] Xu et al. (2019) - https://cvpr2020.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2020/papers/Xu_Free_Parts_Sharp_High-confidence_CVPR_2020_paper.pdf

TITLE: Spatial-Focal Correlation for Improved Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We introduce a spatial-focal correlation module that jointly models the spatial and focal information within a focal stack. Specifically, we propose a novel correlation-based loss that encourages the model to learn meaningful similarities and differences between the focus responses at different focal planes and spatial locations. We then develop a focal-spatial attention mechanism that selectively weights the importance of different focus responses based on their relevance to the current location. Our model, dubbed SpatialFocal Depth Estimation (SFDE), uses these components to learn a more comprehensive representation of the scene and improve depth estimation accuracy.

However, the performance of SFDE may suffer if the correlation module and focal-spatial attention mechanism are not well-tuned, leading to reduced depths accuracy.

PROPOSAL: We revise our previous proposal on expert pruning to focus on improving the pruning algorithm's efficiency and accuracy. We introduce a knowledge distillation-based approach to prune experts, where the target model is a sparse and efficient version of the original DiT model. We train the target model to mimic the output of the original model, allowing us to learn the most important experts and prune the rest, leading to improved accuracy and reduced computational overhead. Additionally, we use a tri-stage pruning strategy, where we first prune experts based on their feature importance, then apply knowledge distillation, and finally refine the pruning through an iterative process. TITLE: Analogous Outcome Rewards for Advantage Collapse Avoidance
PROPOSAL: To address the issue of advantage collapse, we propose a novel reward design that employs analogue outcome rewards for the intermediate turns. PROPOSAL: We propose a novel hierarchical consistency loss function for pre-trained sparse perception models (SPMs) to enhance knowledge transfer across diverse query-based downstream models. TITLE:  Developing Model-Based Data-Quality Selection for Multilingual Pretraining
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of lacking a unified framework for evaluating and selecting pretraining data for multilingual LLMs, we propose a model-based approach where a shared predictor is trained on paired judgment and document embeddings from a multilingualbenchmark dataset, focusing on capturing cross-lingual patterns. This predictor then evaluates the quality of unseen documents, providing a multilingual quality signal. We test this approach on a set of multilingual web crawl samples, seeking to inform downstream LLM performance across languages.
CONTROLS: We compare our model-based selection to existing heuristic and model-based strategies, controlling for performance on language-specific test tasks and robustness to varying levels of sample quality.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: Our model-based selection leads to significant improvements in downstream LLM performance, especially on low-resource languages, however its performance might be limited by noise in the benchmark dataset used for training the predictor.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Investigating Adversarial Training for Model-Based Data Quality Evaluation
PROPOSAL: To improve the robustness of our model-based data-quality evaluation approach, we explore adversarial training as a means to make our predictor less susceptible to sample quality variations. We introduce randomized perturbations to both judgment and document embeddings, accompanied by regularization terms to prevent overfitting, and retrain the predictor under these conditions. This approach enables the predictor to capture more robust features and generalize to unseen data, leading to improved data quality evaluations.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of adversarially trained predictor against its untrained counterpart, as well as against the existing heuristic and model-based strategies, controlling for robustness to varying levels of sample quality and performance on language-specific test tasks.
COST: 5280
PREDICTION: Adversarially training our predictor improves its performance, particularly in low-resource languages, but it might come at the cost of decreased performance on language-specific test tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Evaluating Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer of Data Quality Evaluators
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of adapting data quality evaluators to unseen languages without retraining, we investigate zero-shot cross-lingual transfer of our model-based data quality evaluators. By fine-tuning the shared predictor on a small number of labeled samples from a target language and leveraging cross-lingual embeddings, we aim to extend the applicability of our data quality evaluation approach to new languages without additional training data. We evaluate the performance of zero-shot transfer on a set of multilingual web crawl samples.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of zero-shot transferred predictor against its fully trained counterpart, as well as against the existing heuristic and model-based strategies, controlling for cross-lingual transfer effectiveness and robustness to varying levels of sample quality.
COST: 6720
PREDICTION: Zero-shot cross-lingual transfer enables our data quality evaluator to achieve reasonable performance in unseen languages, but its performance may vary across languages and sample quality might degrade as a result of transfer.

We then evaluate the performance of the pre-trained models on a set of downstream tasks and analyze the effects of data quality on LLM performance.

PREDICTION: Our model-based data quality evaluation approach leads to significant improvements in downstream LLM performance, particularly in languages with limited training data, but its impact may be amplified by the quality of the pretraining data used for the models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigation of Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) Neural Network Pruning
PROPOSAL: 
We investigate whether a one-step generator that combines MLE pruning of a neural network model with a learned mapping of noise tokens to date tokens can compress sampling to a single step. Specifically, we will use the proximal point algorithm (PPA) to sparsify the weights of the teacher AR model, removing tokens with low magnitude and thus neglecting the corresponding probabilities. We will then use a decoder that maps a fixed sequence of noise tokens to the corresponding sparse model's output, and a generator that maps a sequence of noise tokens to the input of the sparse model, and train these three components jointly. This setup should yield a one-step generator that matches the performance of the teacher AR model while significantly reducing computational complexity.
CONTROLS: Baseline comparison with DD1 on standard real-world benchmarks, ablation study of the generator and decoder architectures, control experiment with zero-shot MLE pruning where the proxy point is learned from the same data as the teacher model.
COST: 54000
PREDICTION: This setup should achieve single-step performance comparable to DD1 at a lower computational cost, but the generator may struggle with maintaining the output distribution of the original teacher model, causing performance degradation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Approximating the Conditional Distribution with a Learned Token Quantizer
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a novel approach to learning a one-step generator by directly approximating the conditional distribution over a set of tokens using a learned token quantizer (LTQ). The LTQ is composed of a series of discrete embeddings and binomial output distributions, which are shared cross-conditionally across all positions in the sequence. We will train the LTQ to match the output distribution of the teacher AR model, and use it to reduce the dimensionality of the conditional probability vectors. By jointly training the LTQ with the generator, we can exploit the learned structure of the token quantizer to generate the sequence of tokens in a single forward pass.
CONTROLS: Comparison with DD1 and quantization methods from other fields (e.g., histogram-based quantization), evaluation of the effect of bin size and the use of categorical vs. real-valued embeddings on the performance of the LTQ, ablation study of the discrete embeddings and binomial distributions.
COST: 72000
PREDICTION: This approach should provide a more flexible and scalable alternative to DD1, but the training process may be challenging due to the complex interaction between the LTQ and the generator, and the LTQ's performance may degrade when conditioning on a large number of tokens.
